basic_information.name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
basic_information.creator: Google (Google Cloud / Google DeepMind)
basic_information.release_date: April 9, 2025 (announced at Google Cloud NEXT 2025 in Las Vegas)
basic_information.current_version: 1.24.1 (released February 6, 2026, on PyPI; bi-weekly release cadence)

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: multi_agent | orchestrator | code_first | event_driven — ADK is built on a code-first principle where agents, tools, and orchestration logic are defined directly in code (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java). Supports single-agent and multi-agent hierarchical systems. Workflow agents (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) provide deterministic orchestration, while LlmAgent enables dynamic LLM-driven routing. Agents form tree hierarchies with parent-child relationships for delegation and escalation.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Model-agnostic by design, optimized for Google Gemini. Native support for Gemini models (Gemini 2.0 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini Flash Lite) via Google AI Studio and Vertex AI. Anthropic Claude models (claude-3-sonnet, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) via dedicated model connector. OpenAI models (GPT-4o) via LiteLLM connector. LiteLLM integration provides access to 100+ LLM providers including Cohere, Mistral, local models via Ollama, and any model accessible through Vertex AI Model Garden. Each agent in a hierarchy can use a different model. Important caveat: Google built-in tools (SearchTool, code_execution) only work with Gemini models.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Multi-layered tool integration system. (1) FunctionTool: wraps Python functions as agent tools with automatic schema generation. (2) AgentTool: uses another agent as a tool. (3) Built-in tools: Google Search, code execution (Gemini-only). (4) MCP (Model Context Protocol): native support for consuming MCP server tools and exposing ADK agents as MCP servers. (5) Third-party tool integrations: MCP Toolbox for Databases, custom REST APIs. (6) A2A Protocol: remote agents accessible as tools. Tools support before/after callbacks for validation and monitoring.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: ReAct-style iterative reasoning as core agent loop. ADK includes a planners module for structured planning — agents can break down complex goals into smaller steps before execution. Workflow agents provide deterministic planning: SequentialAgent (linear pipeline), ParallelAgent (concurrent execution), LoopAgent (iterative refinement until condition met). LLM-driven dynamic routing allows the model to select which sub-agent to delegate to based on context. Custom agents can implement arbitrary planning logic by extending BaseAgent.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: First-class multi-agent support — a core design principle. Agents compose into hierarchical trees with parent/child relationships. Three built-in workflow agents: (1) SequentialAgent — assembly-line execution of sub-agents in order, output flows to next agent. (2) ParallelAgent — concurrent execution of independent sub-agents. (3) LoopAgent — repeated execution until exit condition. LLM-driven routing: parent LlmAgent dynamically delegates to child agents based on their descriptions and the current context. Transfer mechanisms: transfer_to_agent for peer transfer, escalate for returning control to parent. A2A protocol enables cross-framework agent-to-agent communication with external agents regardless of their framework.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term | semantic | episodic — (1) Session State: current conversation history and key-value data within a single session, with prefix scoping (app:, user:, temp:). (2) Memory Service: searchable archive spanning across conversations for long-term recall. Two implementations: InMemoryMemoryService (ephemeral) and VertexAiRagMemoryService (persistent via Vertex AI RAG). (3) Artifacts: named, versioned binary data (files, images, audio) associated with sessions or users.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Context is a first-class architectural concept. The Working Context (prompt sent to LLM) is a compiled view — the runtime transforms session state (history, variables, artifacts) into an optimized context window per turn. Context Compaction automatically summarizes older parts of the event history using a sliding window approach, reducing token consumption by 60-80% while maintaining decision quality. Supports custom summarizers via LlmEventSummarizer with configurable AI model for summarization. Compaction operates on the Event stream so sessions remain manageable for long-running conversations.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: in_memory | database | cloud — (1) InMemorySessionService: no persistence, data lost on restart, for development/testing. (2) DatabaseSessionService: async database persistence via SQLite (aiosqlite), PostgreSQL (asyncpg), MySQL (aiomysql). (3) VertexAiSessionService: persistent storage via Google Cloud Vertex AI infrastructure. Artifacts can be stored in Google Cloud Storage (GCS) for persistent binary data across sessions.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context engineering is treated as a core architectural concern. ADK distinguishes between Session (current conversation tracking), State (shared key-value data with scoped prefixes), Memory (cross-session searchable archive), and Artifacts (versioned binary data). The runtime acts as a compiler, transforming raw session data into optimized context windows. Context compaction is built-in and configurable. Prefix system (app:, user:, temp:) enables fine-grained control over state scope and persistence. State updates are always atomic via session_service.append_event() for thread safety.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Code-first agent definition in Python, TypeScript, Go, and Java. Hierarchical multi-agent orchestration with workflow agents (Sequential, Parallel, Loop). LLM-driven dynamic routing between sub-agents. Built-in evaluation system for testing agent behavior against golden datasets (via CLI, pytest, or web UI). Built-in development UI (adk web) for interactive debugging and visual tracing. Context compaction for long conversation management. Artifact management for binary data (files, images, audio). Bidirectional streaming with Gemini Live API for real-time voice and video interaction. Callback system (before_agent, after_agent, before_model, after_model, before_tool, after_tool) for guardrails, monitoring, and behavior customization. Plugin architecture for reusable cross-agent policies. A2A protocol support for cross-framework agent communication. CLI tooling (adk run, adk eval, adk web, adk api_server). OpenTelemetry instrumentation for production observability. Agent-under-100-lines simplicity for basic use cases.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code, voice/audio (bidirectional streaming via Gemini Live API), vision/images (JPEG input), video (frame-based input). Audio input/output supports voice activity detection (VAD) and transcription. Important constraint: response modality must be chosen per session (TEXT or AUDIO), though input can always be multimodal regardless of chosen output modality.
capabilities.autonomy_level: human_in_loop | supervised | fully_autonomous — Configurable per agent and workflow. Default: autonomous within defined scope. Human-in-the-loop implemented via custom tools that pause execution for human input. Callback-based guardrails can block or modify actions based on policies. before_model_callback and before_tool_callback enable pre-approval patterns. Hierarchical agents provide automated oversight via parent agent supervision.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Growing ecosystem. Built-in tools: Google Search (grounding), code execution (Gemini-only). Custom tools via FunctionTool decorator (any Python function). AgentTool for using agents as tools. MCP ecosystem: any MCP-compatible server can provide tools. MCP Toolbox for Databases (Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, etc.). Third-party integrations via A2A protocol. Community tools and samples at google/adk-samples and google/adk-python-community repositories. Awesome-adk-agents curated collection of community templates.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Yes — native, first-class MCP support. ADK agents can both consume tools from external MCP servers and expose themselves as MCP servers. Supports stdio (local) and SSE (remote) connection modes. Configuration is declarative. Enables secure connections between agents and external data sources, tools, and systems via the universal MCP interface.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Yes — native, first-class A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol support. Google co-created the A2A protocol. ADK agents can be exposed as A2A servers via to_a2a() function or adk api_server --a2a CLI command. Auto-generates Agent Cards describing capabilities. RemoteA2aAgent class enables consuming remote A2A agents. Supports A2A v0.2 with stateless interactions and OpenAPI-like authentication. Enables cross-framework agent collaboration regardless of underlying framework.
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: Not natively built-in as a specific feature. ADK uses its own agent configuration system (Python code, instruction strings). However, ADK agents can be configured to read and follow instructions from external files, and AGENTS.md content could be injected into agent instructions via custom setup. Google is a supporter of the AAIF (Agentic AI Foundation) which governs AGENTS.md as an open standard. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Strong interoperability. MCP support enables tool sharing with any MCP-compatible framework (LangChain, CrewAI, Claude, etc.). A2A protocol enables agent communication with any A2A-supporting agent regardless of framework. LiteLLM integration provides universal LLM provider compatibility. Model-agnostic design allows mixing models from different providers within the same agent hierarchy. Can interoperate with LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel agents via A2A. Google Cloud ecosystem integration (Vertex AI, Cloud Run, GKE) provides infrastructure compatibility.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: capability_based | sandbox — Agents are granted specific tools at creation time, defining their capabilities. Callback system provides fine-grained control: before_tool_callback can inspect, modify, or block tool usage based on policies. before_model_callback can validate and filter LLM inputs. Plugin architecture enables reusable security policies across multiple agents. No built-in universal allow/deny list; permissions are scoped per agent through tool assignment and callback logic.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Configurable via multiple mechanisms. (1) Tool-driven escalation: tool_context.actions.escalate = True returns control to parent agent. (2) Custom escalation tools that pause execution and request human input via external systems (UI, ticketing). (3) before_agent_callback can skip agent execution entirely and return a direct response for access control. (4) Callback-based screening using fast models (e.g., Gemini Flash Lite) to triage requests before routing to expensive agents. No built-in structured approval checkpoint mechanism — developers implement escalation logic manually.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Google Search grounding tool provides fact-checking against live web data (Gemini-only). Callback-based output validation via after_model_callback to check model responses against quality standards. Built-in evaluation system allows testing agent outputs against golden datasets to detect hallucinations and regressions. Multi-agent patterns: one agent can validate another's output. Structured output enforcement via Pydantic-style schemas constrains responses. Third-party integration with guardrail tools (e.g., Vijil Dome) for additional protection layers.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Yes — OpenTelemetry instrumentation collects telemetry from agent key actions including prompts, responses, tool calls, and agent transitions. Session event history provides full audit of all actions within a conversation. Built-in adk web UI provides visual trace inspection grouped by user message. Integration with Google Cloud Trace for production audit trails. Third-party observability platforms (Arize, Langfuse, Datadog, AgentOps) provide persistent audit logging.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: pre-approval | post-review | confidence_threshold — (1) Pre-approval via custom tools that pause agent and await human response before proceeding. (2) Post-review via after_model_callback and after_tool_callback for output inspection. (3) Confidence-based routing using callback screening with fast models to triage requests. (4) Sequential workflow pattern: Prepare Agent -> Approval Agent (human review) -> Decision Agent. (5) Hierarchical agent oversight where parent agent supervises child agent outputs. Implementation requires developer setup — no turnkey HITL mechanism.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Google (primary maintainer). Google is a supporter of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation (formed December 2025), which governs open standards like MCP, AGENTS.md, and goose. The A2A protocol is co-developed by Google with industry participation. Apache 2.0 license enables open community contributions.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Creator of A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Protocol — open standard for cross-framework agent communication. Implements MCP (Model Context Protocol) by Anthropic for tool interoperability. Supports OpenTelemetry for observability standardization. Integrates with Vertex AI Agent Engine for managed deployment standards. Contributor to the broader agentic AI open standards ecosystem via AAIF support.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: Deployed on Google Cloud, which itself holds SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and EU compliance certifications. Google Cloud has published EU AI Act compliance guidance. ADK framework itself does not carry independent compliance certifications — compliance depends on deployment environment and configuration. OpenTelemetry audit trails and session logging support regulatory requirements for traceability. On-premise/VPC deployment options via GKE and Cloud Run provide data sovereignty controls. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: cloud | local | hybrid | managed_service | edge — (1) Local: run via adk run, adk web, or Docker/Podman containers for development. (2) Cloud Run: serverless container deployment with auto-scaling from Google Cloud. (3) Vertex AI Agent Engine: fully managed production deployment with end-to-end infrastructure. (4) Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): container orchestration with GPU/TPU support and HorizontalPodAutoscaler. (5) Any container environment: Docker images deployable anywhere. Deployment-agnostic by design.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: horizontal | serverless — Cloud Run provides serverless scaling down to zero (pay-per-use). GKE provides horizontal pod autoscaling based on CPU utilization with GPU/TPU accelerator support. Vertex AI Agent Engine provides managed horizontal scaling. Multi-agent hierarchy enables compositional scaling (add specialized agents as workload grows). Parallel agents enable concurrent execution across multiple sub-agents.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Framework is free and open-source (Apache 2.0). Costs are primarily LLM API costs. Gemini model pricing: Flash Lite at $0.02/1M tokens (cheapest), Gemini 2.0 Flash at moderate pricing, Gemini 2.5 Pro at $5.00/1M output tokens. Google Cloud infrastructure costs depend on deployment mode: Cloud Run (pay-per-request), GKE (cluster costs), Agent Engine (managed service pricing). Enterprise volume discounts of 20-40% available for 100M+ tokens/month. Simple single-agent tasks can cost fractions of a cent with Flash models. Complex multi-agent workflows with Pro models range $0.10-$1.00+ per execution.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Lightweight framework — Python 3.10+ required (also TypeScript/Node.js, Go, Java SDKs available). No GPU required for API-based LLM inference. Local development: standard development machine with 8GB+ RAM. Docker/container deployment: minimal container overhead. GKE production: configurable CPU/GPU/TPU resources via Kubernetes. Agent Engine: managed infrastructure (no user hardware management). Local model inference via Ollama requires appropriate GPU/RAM for chosen model size.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation sends telemetry to Google Cloud project. Google Cloud Trace for distributed tracing. Google Cloud Monitoring integration. Third-party platforms: Arize Phoenix (open-source observability), Datadog LLM Observability (automatic ADK instrumentation, announced Feb 2026), Langfuse, LangWatch, Maxim AI, AgentOps, Freeplay. Each platform adds specialized features: session replay, prompt management, online evaluation, cost tracking.
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — comprehensive tracing built into the framework. adk web UI provides interactive Trace tab with execution flow inspection, automatically grouped by user message. OpenTelemetry traces capture agent reasoning, tool calls, model interactions, and state changes. Google Cloud Trace for production distributed tracing. Third-party trace visualization via Arize, Langfuse, Datadog. Full event history persisted in session for post-hoc analysis.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: production_ready — Deployed on Google Cloud infrastructure with enterprise-grade scaling via Vertex AI Agent Engine. Version 1.24.1 with bi-weekly release cadence indicates active development. Multi-language SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java) suggest production commitment. Google Cloud documentation provides architecture patterns for production single-agent and multi-agent systems. Used in Google Codelabs and enterprise tutorials. However, released less than a year ago (April 2025) — still maturing compared to longer-established frameworks like LangChain.

adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: ~16,200 GitHub stars, ~202 contributors, ~2,600 forks on google/adk-python. Additional repositories: adk-js (TypeScript), adk-go (Go), adk-java (Java), adk-web (developer UI), adk-docs, adk-samples. PyPI package google-adk with regular downloads (exact monthly figures not confirmed). NPM package @google/adk for TypeScript. Active Google Developer Forums and GitHub Discussions community. Multiple Google Codelabs available. Growing ecosystem: awesome-adk-agents community curation. Datadog integration (Feb 2026) signals enterprise adoption traction.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: open-source (Apache 2.0) + pay-for-infrastructure — Framework itself is completely free. Costs come from: (1) LLM API fees (Gemini pricing, or third-party model costs). (2) Google Cloud infrastructure if deploying on Cloud Run, GKE, or Agent Engine (standard GCP pricing). (3) No premium/enterprise tier for the framework itself — enterprise features come through Vertex AI Agent Engine (managed service with its own pricing).
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Customer support automation (multi-agent routing and resolution). Internal AI copilots and assistants. Research and information gathering agents. Data analysis and reporting pipelines. Real-time voice agents (bidirectional streaming with Gemini Live). Multi-system orchestration connecting APIs, databases, and services. Cloud cost analysis and optimization. Document processing and extraction. Multi-agent collaboration across organizational boundaries (via A2A). Enterprise workflow automation with human-in-the-loop approval.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Positioned as Google's primary answer to LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and OpenAI Agents SDK. Key differentiators: (1) Native Google Cloud integration (Vertex AI, Cloud Run, GKE) — strongest for teams already on GCP. (2) Co-creator of A2A protocol — unique cross-framework agent communication. (3) Multi-language support (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java) — broadest language coverage. (4) Built-in evaluation system — evaluation as a first-class feature. (5) Bidirectional streaming for voice/video agents. Weaknesses: (1) Younger than LangChain ecosystem (less mature community). (2) Built-in tools limited to Gemini models. (3) Google ecosystem optimization may feel like soft lock-in. Competes most directly with LangGraph (graph-based control), CrewAI (role-based simplicity), and OpenAI Agents SDK (OpenAI ecosystem).

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: assistant (executes with approval) | autonomous (acts independently) — Configurable. Default behavior is autonomous within defined tool scope. Human-in-the-loop patterns can be implemented via custom tools and callbacks to create approval workflows. Workflow agents can be structured to include mandatory human review stages. The framework does not impose a fixed autonomy level — developers choose the appropriate spectrum position per use case.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Multiple handoff mechanisms available: (1) Tool-driven transfer: tool_context.actions.transfer_to_agent = 'agent_name' transfers control to any named agent regardless of hierarchy position. (2) Tool-driven escalation: tool_context.actions.escalate = True returns control to parent agent up the hierarchy. (3) Human handoff: custom tool pauses execution and sends request to external system (UI, ticketing) waiting for human input, then returns response to agent. (4) A2A handoff: remote agents can be invoked across framework boundaries. (5) Sequential workflow handoff: structured 3-agent pattern (Prepare -> Approval -> Decision) for formal approval chains.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: No built-in RLHF or automated feedback-to-model-improvement pipeline. Evaluation system enables testing against golden datasets to measure and improve agent quality over development cycles. Long-term memory (MemoryService) allows agents to recall past interactions and improve contextual relevance. Session state persistence enables continuity across conversations. Developers iterate by refining instructions, tools, and agent hierarchies based on evaluation results and tracing insights. Third-party observability platforms provide analytics for identifying improvement areas.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: High applicability for startups, especially those on or considering Google Cloud. USE WHEN: (1) You are building on Google Cloud (GCP) — ADK is the most natural fit with seamless Vertex AI, Cloud Run, and GKE integration. (2) You need multi-agent orchestration with clear hierarchy and workflow patterns. (3) You want multi-language support (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java) to match your team's skills. (4) You need real-time voice/video agent capabilities via Gemini Live API. (5) You want built-in evaluation from day one to maintain agent quality. (6) You need cross-framework agent communication via A2A for future interoperability. AVOID WHEN: (1) You are heavily invested in AWS or Azure ecosystems (consider Bedrock Agents or AutoGen). (2) You need maximum community ecosystem breadth right now (LangChain/LangGraph has larger ecosystem). (3) You prefer role-based agent abstractions (CrewAI is more intuitive for business users). (4) You need built-in tools beyond Google Search (Gemini-only limitation). STARTUP ADVANTAGE: Apache 2.0 license means full freedom including commercial use. Framework is free — only pay for LLM API and infrastructure. Google Cloud startup credits ($100k-$350k for Google for Startups program) can fund significant ADK experimentation. Multi-language support means your team can use their strongest language. A2A protocol positions you well for the emerging multi-agent interoperability ecosystem.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUILD with ADK when: your team is on Google Cloud, you have Python/TypeScript/Go developers, you need production-grade multi-agent systems with evaluation, and you want to leverage Gemini models. BUY Vertex AI Agent Engine when: you need managed deployment without DevOps overhead, enterprise scaling, and Google-managed infrastructure. ALTERNATIVES: LangGraph for maximum graph-based control and larger ecosystem, CrewAI for role-based simplicity and rapid prototyping, OpenAI Agents SDK if locked into OpenAI models, AutoGen for research and conversation-heavy workflows. Cost comparison: ADK + Gemini Flash can run simple agents for <$1/day in API costs vs. enterprise managed platforms at $100-$10K+/month.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 4 (AI business models & strategy) — ADK exemplifies Google's open-source-plus-cloud-services strategy (free framework, paid infrastructure). Also relevant to Session 3 (AI project framing — Build vs Buy, framework selection, deployment decisions) and Session 5 (agentic AI architecture, multi-agent patterns, interoperability standards like A2A and MCP).
